en: The Dyad of Being Dissociated from Fetters but Subject to Fettering (Saññojanavippayuttasaññojaniyaduka)

Dependent on a state that is dissociated from the fetters and not conducive to the fetters, there arises a state dissociated from the fetters and not conducive to the fetters by way of root condition.

Dependent on a state dissociated from the fetters and not conducive to the fetters, there arises a state dissociated from the fetters and not non-conducive to the fetters by way of root condition. [Dependent on] a state dissociated from the fetters...

Dependent on a state that is not a fetter-inducing factor, there arise states that are both dissociated from the fetters and not fetter-inducing, as well as states that are dissociated from the fetters and neither fetter-inducing nor non-fetter-inducing,

by way of root condition. Dependent on a state that is dissociated from the fetters and not fetter-inducing, there arises a state that is dissociated from the fetters and neither fetter-inducing nor non-fetter-inducing, by way of root condition.

Dependent on a state that is dissociated from the fetters and not conducive to fetters, as well as a state that is dissociated from the fetters and not conducive to fetters, there arises a state that is dissociated from the fetters and not conducive to fetters by way of root condition. (Abbreviated. Under root condition there are five;
under object condition there are two ... [and so on] ... under non-disappearance condition there are five. (The full detail is given for all.
The Group on Fetters is finished.
